title: V1
name: Controlled advice baseline
summary: Two demographic ODEs isolate deference and maturation under fixed private and adult error distributions.
changes: Initial model: random copying versus weighted judgment; M0 constant fecundity versus the separately prescribed M1 preparation benefit. Analytic growth, equilibrium and conditional invasion maps establish the baseline.
shortcomings: Adult expertise is supplied externally. There is no cultural memory or learning across generations. An M1 interior maturation optimum depends on its imposed tradeoff. Constant maturation hazard is an exponential waiting time, not a birthday. These hypothetical models do not establish a childhood adaptation.

title: V2
name: Improving or decaying advice
summary: Adult advice precision changes with a signed, externally imposed calendar-time drift.
changes: Adds $\sigma_A(t)=\operatorname{clamp}[\sigma_A(0)e^{-gt},\sigma_{\mathrm{floor}},\sigma_{\mathrm{ceiling}}]$. Positive $g$ improves advice; negative $g$ degrades it. Finite-horizon comparisons replace stationary interpretations when advice changes.
shortcomings: Advice quality is still an imposed population-wide curve. It does not arise from individual age, learning, retained knowledge or culture. Frozen-time eigenvalues are not invasion fitness in a changing population. Sampling multiple horizons does not create independent trajectories.

title: V3
name: Declining deference, rising quality
summary: Copying propensity declines over time while an adult advice-quality feature increases.
changes: Adds $d(t)=d_{\mathrm{floor}}+(d_0-d_{\mathrm{floor}})e^{-\lambda_dt}$ and $Q(t)=Q_0+(Q_{\max}-Q_0)(1-e^{-\lambda_Qt})$. The larger factorial separates the two prescribed rates.
shortcomings: Both processes use calendar time, not each individual's developmental age. Neither knowledge acquisition nor inherited adult convictions are modeled. Q is an algebraic modifier, not a cognitive ODE state. A time-varying finite-horizon optimum is not an evolved life history.

title: V4
name: Endogenous culture and selection
summary: Adults transmit beliefs acquired as juveniles; cognitive substates retain confidence and learned trust.
changes: Adds finite cultural confidence, state-preserving maturation, adult correction, public-only and memory controls, a finite RL learner, shared-culture invasion and explicit inherited-trait competition. Adult expertise becomes endogenous.
shortcomings: A bounded endorsement score is not calibrated evidence or psychological dogmatism. The main d combines action substitution and memory acceptance. The oracle has privileged information and finite RL is not all reinforcement learning. Norms, teacher genealogy, source correlation and empirical calibration remain absent.

title: V5
name: Private knowledge and conviction
summary: Separates retained private evidence from held conviction, with noisy access, query costs and actual fact repertoires.
changes: Private-only learners retain childhood knowledge. Action override and social storage are separately ablated. Adult updating, freezing and confidence audits are compared; multi-fact and tutor-confidence experiments plus an exact Bayesian benchmark test stronger alternatives.
shortcomings: Frozen and audit architectures are specified policies. Unit-step finite memory can misweight evidence. Tutor search is cost-free in the companion model. The main load parameter rescales opportunities; independent fact repertoires are not semantic reasoning. A distinct historical dogmatism adaptation remains unsupported.

title: Further work
name: Proposals, not executed models
summary: Research directions motivated by unresolved identification, learning, cultural and demographic questions.
changes: A curated proposal collection linking each extension to a measured limitation of V1–V5. No V6 scientific results or new simulations are claimed.
shortcomings: The proposals are unimplemented. Their suggested predictions can fail. Source dependence, search costs, calibrated trust, richer ecological tasks and empirical validation require new data or experiments.
